Answer.description:
The answer to a question, with what it was built from and what it cost.

**`kind` is declared on both this and `Degraded`, and that is a decision rather than symmetry.** The
two share the 200 status and look alike otherwise, so a client has to be able to tell them apart
without guessing from which fields are present. The service sets `kind` on a degraded payload and
does not set it here, so the default is what a runtime payload will not carry: a client should
branch on `kind == "degraded"` being absent-or-not, and a generated client built from this schema
gets a discriminator it can switch on either way.

denied.description: whether passages outside the role matched
denied.title: Denied

disclosure.description: what this deployment's policy tells a denied user
disclosure.title: Disclosure

kind.description: absent on a real answer; `degraded` on a degradation
kind.title: Kind

model.description: the ROLE, as the manifest names it, not the model that ran
model.title: Model

notice.description: what the user is told about routing, empty when there is nothing to say
notice.title: Notice

resolved_model.description: the provider model behind that role. A client reading only `model` cannot see a manifest swap take effect
resolved_model.title: Resolved Model

trigger.description: which trigger moved it, by name, or empty when none fired
trigger.title: Trigger

unsupported.description: sentences it does not, with the reason
unsupported.title: Unsupported

Answer.title: Answer

BudgetReport.description:
What the deadline did, recorded on every degraded answer.

**`threshold` is null when no threshold tripped**, and that is the honest value: a budget refusal is
not a timeout, and recording one as a threshold would blur the three the design distinguishes.
BudgetReport.title: BudgetReport

Citation.description: One passage the answer could cite. `index` is what the `[n]` markers in the answer refer to.

acl.description: the access label the passage carries; the session's roots must include it
acl.title: Acl

doc_id.description: the document, relative to the deployment's documents root
doc_id.title: Doc Id

Citation.title: Citation

Degraded.description:
The answer when the model will not answer, at HTTP 200.

**`kind` is the field a client must branch on.** An answer and a degradation look alike otherwise,
and a client that renders one as the other shows passages as though the model had written them.
`notice` is absent here and deliberately: the manual records that a degraded payload carries no
notice, which is why the interface probe reads a correct degradation as a silent downgrade.

reason.description: throttled, timeout, budget, unclassified, and the like
reason.title: Reason

threshold.description: which of the three thresholds tripped: first_token, stall, or total
threshold.title: Threshold

Degraded.title: Degraded

Health.description:
Liveness, and what the process actually loaded.

`deployment_id` is how the app knows which deployment answered, which is not decoration on a build
that ships more than once. `status` is `loading` until the registry is read, and a client should say
so rather than treat it as an error.
Health.title: Health

Passage.description: A retrieved passage in a degraded answer, with an excerpt so it can be read without another call.
Passage.title: Passage

Redactions.description:
Kinds and counts of what redaction removed, from the answer and from the question.

A free-form object rather than fixed fields, because the pattern set is a list in
`services/egress/redaction.py` that grows. A client should render whatever keys it is given.
Redactions.title: Redactions

Refusal.description:
A refusal. `kind` is the machine-readable reason; the human wording is in `error`.

**Both are always present**, because the app has to branch on the kind and the person has to read a
sentence. The 403 wording is AIP-211's position: a permission refusal says the permission was denied
or the resource might not exist, which is why it does not simply say "you may not read this".
Refusal.title: Refusal

StreamDegraded.description:
The model could not answer at all. A client that branches only on the events above renders this
as nothing, which reads to a user as an empty answer.
StreamDegraded.title: StreamDegraded

StreamDelta.description: A piece of the answer, **already redacted**. The redaction happens before the frame is emitted.
StreamDelta.title: StreamDelta

StreamDone.description:
The last event. `ttft_ms` is the caller's wait with retrieval included; `model_first_ms` is the
model's own share. The two were once conflated.
StreamDone.title: StreamDone

StreamError.description:
Terminal, because the status code is already spent by the time one of these can be sent.

**`partial_output` is optional because the frames are not uniform.** A timeout reports whether text
had already reached the client; a mid-stream failure reports only its kind. Declaring it as always
present would have been a contract the service does not honour, which is the class of mistake this
whole file exists to stop.
StreamError.title: StreamError

StreamStart.description: Before the model is called. Carries the citations, so a client can show sources immediately.
StreamStart.title: StreamStart

UnsupportedClaim.description: A sentence no retrieved passage backs. Marked rather than dropped, so a client can show it.
UnsupportedClaim.title: UnsupportedClaim

post.description: A question in, a cited answer out.

200.description: A cited answer, or a degraded one at the same status when the model would not answer. **`kind` is what tells them apart**, and a client that renders a degradation as an answer shows retrieved passages as though a model wrote them.

400.description: the body was not JSON, or no question was asked

401.description: no session, an expired one, or a revoked one. The three are one answer on purpose.

403.description: the request supplied its own authority, or the data boundary permits no lane that can answer. The refusal is written to the chain before this returns.

502.description: retrieval failed, or the model could not be reached after the budget was spent

post.description:
The same question, answered in frames.

**Redaction happens here, and it is why this endpoint is not a thin wrapper.** A guardrail that runs after
delivery is audit-only: the bytes are already in the browser. So the response is redacted on the way out
through a holdback buffer sized from the pattern set, and the probe asserts over every frame the client
received rather than over the assembled answer.

Four things are deliberate and each is invisible to a load test: the heartbeat that keeps an idle connection
alive through prompt processing, the `Incremental` and `X-Accel-Buffering` headers that stop a proxy
buffering the stream, the terminal error event that a spent status code makes necessary, and the token count
taken from our own deltas rather than from the gateway, which reports usage in a final chunk an early
disconnect never receives.

schema.title: Response 200 Ask Stream Ask Stream Post

200.description: Server-Sent Events. `event:` is one of `start`, `delta`, `error`, `degraded`, `done`, and `data:` is a JSON object matching the corresponding model here. **A client that branches only on `error` and `delta` renders the `degraded` event as an empty answer**, which is why it is in this list.

400.description: the body was not JSON, or no question was asked

401.description: no session, an expired one, or a revoked one

403.description: **A refusal here is a JSON 403 before the first event, not an SSE error event.** A client that only handles stream events never sees it.

502.description: retrieval failed before the stream began

get.description: Liveness, and what this process actually loaded.

200.description: Liveness, and what the process loaded. `status` is `loading` until the registry is read, which a client should say rather than treat as a fault.
